sentences.zh: 列傳二百三十二

translations.literal: Biographies 232
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 232

sentences.zh: 吳可讀潘敦儼朱一新屠仁守吳兆泰何金壽安維峻

translations.literal: Wu Kedu, Pan Dunyi, Zhu Yixin, Tu Renshou, Wu Zhaotai, He Jinshou, An Weijun
translations.idiomatic: Wu Kedu, Pan Dunyi, Zhu Yixin, Tu Renshou, Wu Zhaotai, He Jinshou, and An Weijun

sentences.zh: 文悌江春霖

translations.literal: Wen Ti, Jiang Chunlin
translations.idiomatic: Wen Ti and Jiang Chunlin

sentences.zh: 吳可讀，字柳堂，甘肅皋蘭人。

translations.literal: Wu Kedu, styled Liutang, was a native of Gaolan in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Kedu, styled Liutang, was from Gaolan in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 初以舉人官伏羌訓導。

translations.literal: At first, as a provincial graduate he served as educational instructor at Fuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He first took office as educational instructor at Fuxiang on the strength of his provincial graduate degree.

sentences.zh: 道光三十年，成進士，授刑部主事。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Daoguang he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In 1850 he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 晉員外郎，遭憂去，主講蘭山書院。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director, then left office on bereavement and became head lecturer at Lanshan Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice director, he left office to mourn a parent and took charge of lecturing at Lanshan Academy.

sentences.zh: 會撒拉番蠢動，被命佐團練。

translations.literal: When the Salar tribes stirred in unrest, he was ordered to assist in organizing local militia.
translations.idiomatic: When the Salar tribes rose in unrest, he was ordered to help organize local militia training.

sentences.zh: 服闋，起故官。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he resumed his former post.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning period ended, he returned to his former post.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部郎中，轉御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to director in the Ministry of Personnel, then made a censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to a directorship in the Ministry of Personnel and then appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 各國使臣請覲，議禮久未決，可讀請免拜跪，時論韙之。

translations.literal: When foreign envoys requested an audience, court ritual was long undecided; Kedu memorialized to exempt them from kneeling and prostration, and public opinion approved.
translations.idiomatic: When foreign envoys sought an audience and court ritual remained unsettled for a long time, Kedu urged that they be excused from kneeling and prostration, and opinion at the time sided with him.

sentences.zh: 烏魯木齊提督成祿誣民為逆，擊殺多人，虛飾胜狀，為左宗棠所劾。

translations.literal: Cheng Lu, military governor of Urumqi, falsely accused the people of rebellion, killed many, and fabricated reports of victory; he was impeached by Zuo Zongtang.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Lu, military governor of Urumqi, falsely branded the people rebels, killed many of them, and fabricated accounts of victory until Zuo Zongtang impeached him.

sentences.zh: 可讀繼陳其罪有可斬者十，不可緩者五，尋逮問，讞上論斬，廷臣請改監候。

translations.literal: Kedu followed with ten capital offenses and five that brooked no delay; Cheng was soon arrested and tried, the verdict called for execution, and court officials asked that it be changed to imprisonment awaiting execution.
translations.idiomatic: Kedu went on to list ten offenses warranting execution and five that could not be delayed. Cheng was soon arrested and tried; when the verdict recommended death, court officials asked that the sentence be commuted to imprisonment awaiting execution.

sentences.zh: 可讀憤甚，复疏爭：「請斬成祿以謝甘民，再斬臣以謝成祿。

translations.literal: Kedu was deeply angered and memorialized again in protest: "I beg that Cheng Lu be executed to appease the people of Gansu, and that I be executed next to appease Cheng Lu."
translations.idiomatic: Furious, Kedu memorialized again: "I beg that Cheng Lu be executed to appease the people of Gansu, and that I be executed afterward to appease Cheng Lu."

sentences.zh: 」語過戇直，被訶責，鐫三級。

translations.literal: " His words were excessively blunt; he was rebuked and demoted three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: " His language was recklessly blunt; he was rebuked and demoted three ranks.

sentences.zh: 歸，复掌教蘭山。

translations.literal: He returned home and again took charge of teaching at Lanshan.
translations.idiomatic: He went home and again headed teaching at Lanshan.

sentences.zh: 逾年，穆宗崩，德宗纘業，起吏部主事。

translations.literal: After a year the Muzong Emperor died and the Dezong Emperor succeeded; Kedu was recalled as a secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, after Emperor Muzong died and Emperor Dezong took the throne, Kedu was recalled as a secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 光緒五年，穆宗奉安惠陵，自請隨赴襄禮。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Guangxu, when Muzong was interred at Huiling, he volunteered to go and assist in the rites.
translations.idiomatic: In 1879, when Emperor Muzong was laid to rest at Huiling, he volunteered to accompany the procession and assist in the burial rites.

sentences.zh: 還次薊州，宿廢寺，自縊，未絕，仰藥死，於懷中得遺疏，則請為穆宗立嗣也。

translations.literal: On the return he stopped at Jizhou, lodged in an abandoned temple, hanged himself; before he died he took poison, and from his breast was found a final memorial asking that an heir be established for Muzong.
translations.idiomatic: On the way back he halted at Jizhou and lodged in a ruined temple. He hanged himself; before life left him he took poison as well. A final memorial found on his person asked that an heir be appointed for Emperor Muzong.

sentences.zh: 其言曰：「罪臣聞治不諱亂，安不忘危。

translations.literal: It read: "This guilty official has heard that in governing one does not shrink from disorder, and in security one does not forget danger."
translations.idiomatic: It read: "Your guilty servant has heard that good government does not shrink from speaking of disorder, and security must not forget danger."

sentences.zh: 危亂而可諱忘，則進苦口於堯舜，為無疾呻吟，陳隱患於聖明，為不祥舉動。

translations.literal: If danger and disorder may be concealed and forgotten, then offering bitter counsel to Yao and Shun would be feigned groaning without illness, and setting forth hidden perils before the sage would be an ill-omened act.
translations.idiomatic: If danger may be hushed up and forgotten, then offering bitter counsel even to Yao and Shun would be called feigned groaning without illness, and warning of hidden perils before a sage ruler would be deemed an ill-omened act.

sentences.zh: 罪臣前因言事獲譴，蒙我先皇帝曲賜矜全，免臣以斬而死，以囚而死，以傳訊觸忌而死。

translations.literal: This guilty official was once punished for remonstrance, yet my late emperor graciously spared me, sparing me death by execution, death in prison, and death for giving offense in interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: I was once punished for speaking out, yet my late emperor graciously spared me—spared me execution, imprisonment unto death, and death for giving offense under interrogation.

sentences.zh: 犯三死而未死，不求生而再生，則今日罪臣未盡之餘年，皆我先皇帝數年前所賜也。

translations.literal: Having incurred three deaths yet not dying, and not seeking life only to live again, the remaining years of this guilty official today are all years my late emperor granted years ago.
translations.idiomatic: Having faced three deaths yet lived, and not seeking life merely to live on, whatever years remain to me now are years my late emperor granted me years ago.

sentences.zh: 欽奉兩宮皇太后懿旨，以醇親王之子承繼文宗顯皇帝為子，入承大統為嗣皇帝，俟嗣皇帝生有皇子，即承繼大行皇帝為嗣。

translations.literal: By the august command of the two empress dowagers, the son of Prince Chun was adopted as son to the Xian Emperor Wenzong, entered the succession as heir emperor, and when the heir emperor should have a son, that son would succeed the late emperor as heir.
translations.idiomatic: By decree of the two empress dowagers, the son of Prince Chun was adopted as heir to Emperor Wenzong, ascended the throne as successor emperor, and when he should have a son of his own, that son would succeed the late emperor in turn.

sentences.zh: 我皇上仁孝性成，承我兩宮皇太后授以寶位，將來千秋萬歲時，必能以我兩宮皇太后今日之心為心。

translations.literal: Our emperor is filial and benevolent by nature; receiving the throne from the two empress dowagers, in ages to come he will surely keep their hearts of today as his own.
translations.idiomatic: Our emperor is filial and benevolent by nature. Having received the throne from the two empress dowagers, in time to come he will surely hold the same intentions they hold today.

sentences.zh: 而在廷之忠佞不齊，即眾論之異同不一。

translations.literal: Yet at court loyal and treacherous are not alike, and public opinion is not of one mind.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at court the loyal and the treacherous are not alike, and public opinion is divided.

sentences.zh: 以宋初宰相趙普之賢，而猶首背杜太后；

translations.literal: For all the worth of the early Song minister Zhao Pu, he was still foremost in going against Empress Dowager Du;
translations.idiomatic: For all the worth of Zhao Pu, chief minister in the early Song, he was still foremost in defying Empress Dowager Du;

sentences.zh: 以明大學士王直之為舊臣，而猶以黃𤥠請立景帝太子一疏不出我輩為愧。

translations.literal: For all that Wang Zhi of the Ming was a grand secretary and an old minister, he still took shame that Huang Hong's memorial to establish the Jing Emperor's crown prince did not come from our party.
translations.idiomatic: For all that Wang Zhi of the Ming was a grand secretary and a veteran minister, he still felt ashamed that Huang Hong's memorial to establish the Jing Emperor's crown prince had not come from men like us.

sentences.zh: 賢者如此，遑問不肖？

translations.literal: If the worthy are thus, how much more the unworthy?
translations.idiomatic: If even the worthy behave thus, what may be expected of the unworthy?

sentences.zh: 舊人如此，奚責新進？

translations.literal: If old hands are thus, how can new men be blamed?
translations.idiomatic: If veterans act thus, how can newcomers be blamed?

sentences.zh: 名位已定者如此，況在未定。

translations.literal: If those whose titles and positions are fixed are thus, how much more when they are not yet fixed.
translations.idiomatic: If even those whose rank is already settled behave thus, how much more when it is not yet settled.

sentences.zh: 惟有仰求我兩宮皇太后再降諭旨，將來大統，仍歸大行皇帝嗣子，嗣皇帝雖百斯男，中外臣工均不得以異言進。

translations.literal: I can only humbly beg the two empress dowagers to issue another decree: that hereafter the succession return to a son of the late emperor, and that though the heir emperor have a hundred sons, officials within and without may not advance dissenting views.
translations.idiomatic: I can only humbly beg the two empress dowagers to issue another decree: that hereafter the succession remain with a son of the late emperor, and that even if the reigning emperor should have a hundred sons, no official at court or in the provinces may advance a contrary opinion.

sentences.zh: 如此，則猶是本朝子以傳子之家法，而我大行皇帝未有子而有子，即我兩宮皇太后未有孫而有孫，異日繩繩揖揖相引於萬代者，皆我兩宮皇太后所自出而不可移易者也。

translations.literal: Thus it would still be this dynasty's house law of father passing the throne to son; the late emperor would have no son yet have a son, and the two empress dowagers would have no grandson yet have a grandson; the line stretching through ten thousand generations would all spring from the two empress dowagers and could not be altered.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the dynasty's house law of father passing the throne to son would be preserved. The late emperor would have no son and yet have a son; the two empress dowagers would have no grandson and yet have a grandson. The line that would stretch in orderly succession through ten thousand generations would all spring from the two empress dowagers and could not be altered.

sentences.zh: 彼時罪臣即欲有言，繼思降調不得越職言事。

translations.literal: At that time this guilty official wished to speak, but then reflected that after demotion one might not remonstrate outside one's office.
translations.idiomatic: At that time I wished to speak out, but then reflected that after demotion one might not remonstrate outside one's proper office.

sentences.zh: 今逢我大行皇帝奉安山陵，恐積久漸忘，則罪臣昔日所留以有待者，今則迫不及待矣。

translations.literal: Now, as the late emperor is laid to rest in the hills, I fear that with time this will be forgotten; what this guilty official once reserved and waited for can no longer wait.
translations.idiomatic: Now, as the late emperor is laid to rest in the hills, I fear that with time this matter will be forgotten. What I once held back and waited to say can wait no longer.

sentences.zh: 謹以我先皇帝所賜餘年，為我先皇帝上乞數行懿旨，惟望我兩宮皇太后、我皇上憐其哀鳴，勿以為無疾呻吟、不祥舉動，則罪臣雖死無憾。

translations.literal: I respectfully use the remaining years my late emperor granted to beg on his behalf for a few lines of august decree, only hoping the two empress dowagers and our emperor will pity this lament and not deem it feigned groaning or an ill-omened act; then this guilty official may die without regret.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully use the remaining years my late emperor granted me to beg on his behalf for a few lines of decree, praying only that the two empress dowagers and our emperor will pity this cry of grief and not dismiss it as feigned groaning or an ill-omened act. Then I may die without regret.

sentences.zh: 尤原我兩宮皇太后、我皇上體聖祖、世宗之心，調劑寬猛，養忠厚和平之福，任用老成；

translations.literal: I further pray the two empress dowagers and our emperor take to heart the minds of the Kangxi and Yongzheng emperors, balance severity and leniency, nurture the blessing of loyalty and peace, and employ seasoned men;
translations.idiomatic: I further pray that the two empress dowagers and our emperor take to heart the spirit of the Kangxi and Yongzheng emperors, balance severity and leniency, nurture the blessings of loyalty and peace, and employ seasoned men;

sentences.zh: 毋爭外國之所獨爭，為中華留不盡；

translations.literal: do not contend for what foreign states alone contend for, and leave inexhaustible reserves for China;
translations.idiomatic: do not contend for what foreign powers alone contend over, and leave inexhaustible reserves for China;

sentences.zh: 毋創祖宗之所未創，為子孫留有餘。

translations.literal: do not create what the ancestors never created, and leave surplus for posterity.
translations.idiomatic: do not innovate what the ancestors never innovated, and leave a surplus for posterity.

sentences.zh: 罪臣言畢於斯，命畢於斯，謹以大統所繫上聞。

translations.literal: This guilty official's words end here and his life ends here; I respectfully report what concerns the succession.
translations.idiomatic: My words end here and my life ends here. I respectfully report what concerns the succession to the throne.

sentences.zh: 」吏部奏諸朝，詔憫其忠，予優恤。

translations.literal: " The Ministry of Personnel reported to the court; an edict commiserated his loyalty and granted generous condolence.
translations.idiomatic: " The Ministry of Personnel reported the matter to court. An edict commiserated his loyalty and granted generous posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 下群臣議，遂定以繼德宗之統為穆宗之子，無異論。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the ministers for discussion, and it was settled without dissent that the succession to Dezong would be as son to Muzong.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the ministers for discussion, and without dissent it was settled that the succession to Emperor Dezong would be as son to Emperor Muzong.

sentences.zh: 可讀臨歿遺書與其子之桓，謂出薊州一步即非死所。

translations.literal: On the verge of death Kedu left a letter to his son Zhihuan, saying that one step beyond Jizhou would not be the place to die.
translations.idiomatic: On the verge of death Kedu left a letter to his son Zhihuan, saying that one step beyond Jizhou would not be the place to die.

sentences.zh: 之桓遂成其遺志，葬薊州。

translations.literal: Zhihuan then fulfilled his father's last wish and buried him at Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhihuan then fulfilled his father's last wish and buried him at Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 都人即所居城南舊宅祠祀之。

translations.literal: The people of the capital set up a shrine to him at his old residence south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the capital established a shrine to him at his old residence south of the city.

sentences.zh: 有潘敦儼者，字清畏，籍江寧，總督鐸子。

translations.literal: There was Pan Dunyi, styled Qingwei, registered in Jiangning, son of Governor-General Duo.
translations.idiomatic: There was Pan Dunyi, styled Qingwei, registered in Jiangning and son of Governor-General Duo.

sentences.zh: 以任子官工部郎中，遷御史。

translations.literal: By hereditary privilege he served as director in the Ministry of Works, then was transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he served as a director in the Ministry of Works and was later made censor.

sentences.zh: 默念穆宗嗣統未有定議，孝哲毅皇后又仰藥殉，遂疏請表揚穆後潛德，更諡號，並解醇親王奕枻職任，詔嚴斥奪職。

translations.literal: Brooding that Muzong's succession was unsettled and that Empress Xiaozheyi had taken poison in martyrdom, he memorialized to honor the late empress's hidden virtue, change her posthumous title, and remove Prince Chun Yixuan from office; an edict sternly rebuked him and stripped him of his post.
translations.idiomatic: Brooding over the unsettled succession to Emperor Muzong and Empress Xiaozheyi's death by poison in devotion to her husband, he memorialized to honor the late empress's hidden virtues, revise her posthumous title, and remove Prince Chun Yixuan from office. An edict sternly rebuked him and stripped him of his post.

sentences.zh: 歸隱於酒，閱二十餘年，卒。

translations.literal: He retired and hid himself in drink; after more than twenty years he died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired and took refuge in drink. More than twenty years later he died.

sentences.zh: 朱一新，字蓉生，浙江義烏人。

translations.literal: Zhu Yixin, styled Rongsheng, was a native of Yiwu in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yixin, styled Rongsheng, was from Yiwu in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 鄉舉對策語觸時忌，主司李文田特拔之。

translations.literal: In the provincial examination his policy essay touched taboos of the time; chief examiner Li Wentian specially advanced him.
translations.idiomatic: In the provincial examination his policy essay touched contemporary taboos, but chief examiner Li Wentian specially advanced him.

sentences.zh: 入貲為內閣中書。

translations.literal: He purchased office as a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He purchased office as a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，成進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1876 he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 法越事起，數上書主戰，又嘗畫海防策，語至切要。

translations.literal: When the Franco-Vietnamese affair arose, he repeatedly memorialized in favor of war; he also once drafted a coastal defense plan, its language most urgent and essential.
translations.idiomatic: When the Franco-Vietnamese conflict broke out, he repeatedly memorialized in favor of war. He also once drafted a coastal defense plan whose language was urgent and to the point.

sentences.zh: 典湖北鄉試，稱得士。

translations.literal: He presided over the Hubei provincial examination and was praised for selecting worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over the Hubei provincial examination and was praised for selecting worthy candidates.

sentences.zh: 十一年，轉御史，連上封事，言論侃侃，不避貴戚。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was made censor; he submitted successive sealed memorials, speaking forthrightly without shunning powerful kin.
translations.idiomatic: In 1885 he was made censor. He submitted successive sealed memorials, speaking forthrightly without shunning powerful families.

sentences.zh: 內侍李蓮英漸著聲勢。

translations.literal: The palace eunuch Li Lianying gradually grew prominent in power.
translations.idiomatic: The palace eunuch Li Lianying gradually grew prominent in influence.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，醇親王奕枻閱海軍，蓮英從，一新憂之。

translations.literal: After a year Prince Chun Yixuan inspected the navy and Lianying accompanied him; Yixin was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Prince Chun Yixuan inspected the navy with Lianying in attendance, and Yixin was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 而適值山東患河，燕、晉、蜀、閩患水，遂以遇災修省為言，略曰：「我朝家法，嚴馭宦寺。

translations.literal: It happened that Shandong suffered from the Yellow River, and Yan, Jin, Shu, and Min from floods; he therefore spoke under the rubric of meeting disaster with self-examination, saying in part: "Our dynasty's house law strictly controls eunuchs."
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Shandong was afflicted by the Yellow River and Yan, Jin, Shu, and Min by floods. He therefore spoke under the rubric of meeting disaster with self-examination, saying in part: "Our dynasty's house law strictly controls eunuchs."

sentences.zh: 世祖宮中立鐵牌，更億萬年，昭為法守。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor set up an iron tablet in the palace to stand for ten thousand ages as a declared law to be kept.
translations.idiomatic: The Shizu Emperor set up an iron tablet in the palace to stand for ten thousand ages as a declared law to be kept.

sentences.zh: 聖母垂簾，安得海假採辦出京，立寘重典。

translations.literal: When the Holy Mother held the curtain, how could An Dehai on the pretext of procurement leave the capital? He was at once punished by heavy statute.
translations.idiomatic: When the Holy Mother held court from behind the curtain, how could An Dehai leave the capital on the pretext of procurement? He was at once punished under the severest statute.

sentences.zh: 皇上登極，張得喜等情罪尤重，謫配為奴。

translations.literal: When our emperor ascended the throne, Zhang Dexi and others, their offenses still graver, were banished and enslaved.
translations.idiomatic: When our emperor ascended the throne, Zhang Dexi and others, whose offenses were still graver, were banished and enslaved.

sentences.zh: 是以綱紀肅然，罔敢恣肆。

translations.literal: Thus discipline was stern and none dared act wantonly.
translations.idiomatic: Thus discipline was stern and none dared act wantonly.

sentences.zh: 乃今夏巡閱海軍之役，太監李蓮英隨至天津，道路譁傳，士庶駴愕，意深宮或別有不得已苦衷，匪外廷所能喻。

translations.literal: Yet this summer, in the naval inspection, the eunuch Li Lianying followed to Tianjin; the roads buzzed with rumor and gentry and commoners were startled, thinking the inner palace might have some unavoidable hardship that the outer court could not comprehend.
translations.idiomatic: Yet this summer, during the naval inspection, the eunuch Li Lianying followed to Tianjin. Rumor spread along the roads and gentry and commoners were startled, thinking the inner palace might have some unavoidable hardship that the outer court could not comprehend.

sentences.zh: 然宗籓至戚，閱軍大典，而令刑餘之輩《廣則》乎其間，其將何以詰戎兵崇體制？

translations.literal: Yet for a prince of the imperial clan, a kinsman of the first rank, at a great ceremony of inspecting the army, to let mutilated men take part in it—how may troops be disciplined and the system honored?
translations.idiomatic: Yet for a prince of the imperial clan, a kinsman of the first rank, at a great ceremony of inspecting the army, to let eunuchs take part in it—how may troops be disciplined and institutional dignity upheld?

sentences.zh: 況作法於涼，其弊猶貪。

translations.literal: Moreover, if one sets the pattern in a cool season, the resulting abuse will still be greed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, as the proverb says, if one sets the pattern in a cool season, the resulting abuse will still be greed.

sentences.zh: 唐之監軍，豈其本意，積漸者然也。

translations.literal: The Tang practice of supervising armies—was that its original intent? It came about through gradual accretion.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang practice of eunuch army supervisors—was that its original intent? It came about through gradual accretion.

translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zhidong governed Guangdong he founded Guangya Academy and invited Yixin to serve as head lecturer.

translations.idiomatic: Yixin was broadly read and thoroughly versed in the methods of the Han, Song, and Ming Confucian schools, striving to master the classics for practical application.

translations.idiomatic: Students who were clever and fond of novelty he always guided back to solid and upright ways. His words are collected in his Wuxie Tang Dawen.

translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of forty-nine.

translations.idiomatic: Tu Renshou, styled Meijun, was from Xiaogan in Hubei.

translations.idiomatic: In 1874 he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.

translations.idiomatic: During the Guangxu reign he was made censor.

translations.idiomatic: When policy issued from many quarters, Renshou, citing heaven's warnings, asked to repair government and listed six items: stop evasion of responsibility, open what is blocked, be cautious in action, restrain familiar attendants, pity the people's afflictions, and give weight to state finance—all rooted in great impartiality and in revering heaven and laboring for the people. translations.idiomatic: He also spoke of rewards offered for naval contributions to the court, indiscriminate advancement without order, and a growing tide of opportunists.

translations.idiomatic: Renshou painfully set forth five abuses: qualifications and seniority ignored—the first abuse;

translations.idiomatic: titles and offices recklessly bestowed—the second abuse;

translations.idiomatic: reward and punishment inverted—the third abuse;

translations.idiomatic: seeking gain yet suffering loss, state finance turning to deficit—the fourth abuse;

translations.idiomatic: brokers and cliques encroaching, beyond investigation—the fifth abuse.

translations.literal: When the five abuses flourished, three perils arose: peril to the afflicted people, peril of obstructing the worthy, and peril of ruining discipline and law.
translations.idiomatic: When the five abuses flourished, three perils arose: peril to the afflicted people, peril of obstructing the worthy, and peril of ruining discipline and law.

translations.literal: " Because it came down from the Naval Yamen and was carried out by august command, none dared rashly report it; thus slander filled the streets while the court did not hear, perils lay hidden in minute matters while the court did not know, petty men had their way, and favor and bribes spread.

sentences.zh: 若不停止，即承平無事，猶或召亂，況時局孔艱乎？

translations.idiomatic: If this is not stopped, even in untroubled peace disorder may be summoned—how much more when the times are desperately hard?

translations.idiomatic: After returning home he became head lecturer at Lingde Hall in Shanxi.

translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he died.

translations.idiomatic: He was friendly with Renshou, and they urged each other on in duty and righteousness.

translations.idiomatic: National defense was neglected and the navy especially weak; the court diverted its funds to repair the Summer Palace.

translations.idiomatic: After returning home he successively headed lecturing at Longquan and Jingxin academies and served as chairman of the public education council.

translations.idiomatic: He went out as educational commissioner of Henan, then returned to serve as lecturer on the Daily Lectures and Records of the Emperor.

translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Zuo Zongtang and others reported his case to court, saying he had the air of the ancient upright officials.

translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Weijun memorialized: "Li Hongzhang on ordinary days uses foreign powers to magnify himself and plainly does not wish war; whoever speaks of war is at once rebuked."

translations.literal: "Why?"
translations.idiomatic: "Why?"

sentences.zh: 皇太后既歸政，若仍遇事牽制，將何以上對祖宗，下對天下臣民？

translations.literal: "If the empress dowager has returned power, yet still restrains affairs at every turn, how may she face the ancestors above or the officials and people below?"
translations.idiomatic: "If the empress dowager has returned power, yet still restrains affairs at every turn, how may she face the ancestors above or the officials and people below?"

sentences.zh: 至李蓮英是何人斯，敢干政事乎？

translations.literal: "As for Li Lianying—who is he to dare meddle in government?"
translations.idiomatic: "As for Li Lianying—who is he to dare meddle in government?"

sentences.zh: 如果屬實，律以祖宗法制，豈復可容？

translations.literal: "If this is true, judged by the ancestral laws, how could he still be tolerated?"
translations.idiomatic: "If this is true, judged by the ancestral laws, how could he still be tolerated?"

sentences.zh: 唯是朝廷受李鴻章哃喝，不及詳審，而樞臣中或系私黨，甘心左袒，或恐決裂，姑事調停。

translations.literal: "Only the court is cowed by Li Hongzhang and cannot examine matters fully, while among grand councilors some belong to private factions and willingly take his side, or fear a break and for the moment mediate."
translations.idiomatic: "Only the court is cowed by Li Hongzhang and cannot examine matters fully, while among grand councilors some belong to private factions and willingly take his side, or fear a break and for the moment mediate."

sentences.zh: 李鴻章事事挾制朝廷，抗違諭旨。

translations.literal: "Li Hongzhang on every matter coerces the court and resists imperial edicts."
translations.idiomatic: "Li Hongzhang on every matter coerces the court and resists imperial edicts."

sentences.zh: 唯冀皇上赫然震怒，明正其罪，佈告天下，如是而將士有不奮興、賊人有不破滅者，即請斬臣以正妄言之罪。

translations.literal: "I only hope Your Majesty will be greatly angered, clearly punish his crime, and proclaim it to all the realm; if after this the officers and men do not rouse themselves and the enemy is not destroyed, then I beg that I be executed to correct the crime of reckless speech."
translations.idiomatic: "I only hope Your Majesty will be greatly angered, clearly punish his crime, and proclaim it to all the realm; if after this the officers and men do not rouse themselves and the enemy is not destroyed, then I beg that I be executed to correct the crime of reckless speech."

sentences.zh: 」疏入，上諭：「軍國要事，仰承懿訓遵行，天下共諒。

translations.literal: "When the memorial entered, an imperial rescript said: "On military and state affairs we follow august instruction; all the realm understands."
translations.idiomatic: "When the memorial entered, an imperial rescript said: "On military and state affairs we follow august instruction; all the realm understands."

sentences.zh: 乃安維峻封奏，託諸傳聞，竟有'皇太后遇事牽制'之語，妄言無忌，恐開離間之端。

translations.literal: "Yet An Weijun's sealed memorial, resting on rumor, actually has the words 'the empress dowager restrains affairs at every turn'; reckless speech without restraint may open a breach of estrangement."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet An Weijun's sealed memorial, resting on rumor, actually has the words 'the empress dowager restrains affairs at every turn'; reckless speech without restraint may open a breach of estrangement."

sentences.zh: 」命革職發軍台。

translations.literal: "He was ordered stripped of office and sent to the military garrison."
translations.idiomatic: "He was ordered stripped of office and sent to the military garrison."

sentences.zh: 維峻以言獲罪，直聲震中外，人多榮之。

translations.literal: Weijun was punished for his words; his upright reputation shook China and abroad, and many honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Weijun was punished for his words; his upright reputation shook China and abroad, and many honored him.

sentences.zh: 訪問者萃於門，餞送者塞於道，或贈以言，或資以贐，車馬飲食，眾皆為供應。

translations.literal: Visitors gathered at his gate and farewell parties filled the road; some gave words, some supplied travel money, and for carriage, food, and drink all provided.
translations.idiomatic: Visitors gathered at his gate and farewell parties filled the road; some gave words, some supplied travel money, and for carriage, food, and drink all provided.

sentences.zh: 抵戍所，都統以下皆敬以客禮，聘主講掄才書院。

translations.literal: On reaching the garrison post, all from the military governor down treated him with guest ceremony and engaged him to lecture at the Luncai Academy.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the garrison post, all from the military governor down treated him with guest ceremony and engaged him to lecture at the Luncai Academy.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，釋還，遂歸里。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was released and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1899 he was released and returned home.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，起授內閣侍讀，充京師大學總教習。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he was recalled as reader in the Grand Secretariat and made chief instructor of the Capital University.
translations.idiomatic: In 1908 he was recalled as reader in the Grand Secretariat and made chief instructor of the Capital University.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年，复辭歸。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuantong he again begged leave and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In 1911 he again begged leave and returned.

sentences.zh: 越十有五年，卒。

translations.literal: After more than fifteen years he died.
translations.idiomatic: After more than fifteen years he died.

sentences.zh: 維峻崇樸實，尚​​踐履，不喜為博辨，尤嚴義利之分。

translations.literal: Weijun honored plainness and practicality, valued conduct over disputation, and especially kept strict the boundary between righteousness and profit.
translations.idiomatic: Weijun honored plainness and practicality, valued conduct over disputation, and especially kept strict the boundary between righteousness and profit.

sentences.zh: 歸後退隱柏崖，杜門著書，隱然以名教綱常為己任。

translations.literal: After returning he retired to Baiya, closed his door and wrote books, and quietly took the norms of teaching and human relations as his charge.
translations.idiomatic: After returning he retired to Baiya, closed his door and wrote books, and quietly took the norms of teaching and human relations as his charge.

sentences.zh: 每談及世變，輒憂形於色，卒抑鬱以終。

translations.literal: Whenever he spoke of the changes of the age, worry showed on his face; he ended in depression.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he spoke of the changes of the age, worry showed on his face; he ended in depression.

sentences.zh: 著有四書講義、詩文集。

translations.literal: He wrote Expositions on the Four Books and collected poems and prose.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Expositions on the Four Books and collected poems and prose.

sentences.zh: 文悌，字仲恭，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Wen Ti, styled Zhonggong, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Ti, styled Zhonggong, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 以筆帖式歷戶部郎中，出為河南知府，改御史。

translations.literal: From clerk he rose through director in the Ministry of Revenue, went out as prefect of Henan, and was changed to censor.
translations.idiomatic: From clerk he rose through director in the Ministry of Revenue, went out as prefect of Henan, and was changed to censor.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十四年，變法詔下，禮部主事王照應詔上言，尚書許應騤不為代奏。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Guangxu, when the reform edict was issued, Wang Zhao of the Ministry of Rites responded to the edict with a memorial, but Minister Xu Yingkui did not transmit it.
translations.idiomatic: In 1898, when the reform edict was issued, Wang Zhao of the Ministry of Rites responded to the edict with a memorial, but Minister Xu Yingkui did not transmit it.

sentences.zh: 御史宋伯魯、楊深秀聯名劾以守舊迂謬，阻撓新政，諭應騤明白回奏，覆奏稱珍惜名器，物色通才，並辭連工部主事康有為，請罷斥驅逐。

translations.literal: Censors Song Bolu and Yang Shenxiu jointly impeached him for conservatism and obstruction of the new policies; the throne ordered Xu to reply clearly, and in reply he spoke of cherishing offices and seeking able men, also implicating Kang Youwei of the Ministry of Works and asking that he be dismissed and driven out.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Song Bolu and Yang Shenxiu jointly impeached him for conservatism and obstruction of the new policies; the throne ordered Xu to reply clearly, and in reply he spoke of cherishing offices and seeking able men, also implicating Kang Youwei of the Ministry of Works and asking that he be dismissed and driven out.

sentences.zh: 奏上，以抑格言路，首違詔旨，禮部尚書、侍郎皆革職，賞照四品京堂。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, for suppressing free speech and first violating the edict, the minister and vice ministers of Rites were all dismissed and Wang was rewarded with fourth-rank capital office.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, for suppressing free speech and first violating the edict, the minister and vice ministers of Rites were all dismissed and Wang was rewarded with fourth-rank capital office.

sentences.zh: 文悌以言官為人指使，黨庇報復，紊亂臺諫，遂上疏言：「康有為向不相識，忽踵門求謁，送以所著書籍，閱其著作，以變法為宗。

translations.literal: Wen Ti, as a remonstrating official acting at others' direction, factionally shielded revenge and confused the censorate, and therefore memorialized: "Kang Youwei was previously unknown to me when he suddenly came to my door seeking an audience and presented his writings; reading them, I found reform to be his doctrine."
translations.idiomatic: Wen Ti, as a remonstrating official acting at others' direction, factionally shielded revenge and confused the censorate, and therefore memorialized: "Kang Youwei was previously unknown to me when he suddenly came to my door seeking an audience and presented his writings; reading them, I found reform to be his doctrine."

sentences.zh: 而尤堪駭詫者，託辭孔子改制，謂孔子作春秋西狩獲麟為受命之符，以春秋變週為孔子當一代王者。

translations.literal: "What is still more shocking is that under the pretext of Confucius' reform he says Confucius, when the Spring and Autumn Annals records the capture of the lin west of the hunt, took it as a token of receiving the mandate, and that changing Zhou through the Spring and Autumn means Confucius should be king of an age."
translations.idiomatic: "What is still more shocking is that under the pretext of Confucius' reform he says Confucius, when the Spring and Autumn Annals records the capture of the lin west of the hunt, took it as a token of receiving the mandate, and that changing Zhou through the Spring and Autumn means Confucius should be king of an age."

sentences.zh: 明似推崇孔子，實則自申其改制之義。

translations.literal: "Outwardly he seems to honor Confucius; in fact he expounds his own doctrine of reform."
translations.idiomatic: "Outwardly he seems to honor Confucius; in fact he expounds his own doctrine of reform."

sentences.zh: 乃知康有為之學術，正如漢書嚴助所謂以春秋為蘇秦縱橫者耳。

translations.literal: "Thus Kang Youwei's learning is just as Yan Zhu in the Book of Han said of using the Spring and Autumn for Su Qin's vertical and horizontal alliances."
translations.idiomatic: "Thus Kang Youwei's learning is just as Yan Zhu in the Book of Han said of using the Spring and Autumn for Su Qin's vertical and horizontal alliances."

sentences.zh: 及聆其談治術，則專主西學，以師法日本為良策。

translations.literal: "When I heard him discuss statecraft, he exclusively advocated Western learning and taking Japan as teacher as the good policy."
translations.idiomatic: "When I heard him discuss statecraft, he exclusively advocated Western learning and taking Japan as teacher as the good policy."

sentences.zh: 如近來時務、知新等報所論，尊俠力，伸民權，興黨會，改制度，甚則欲去拜跪之禮儀，廢滿、漢之文字，平君臣之尊卑，改男女之外內。

translations.literal: "As recent papers such as Current Affairs and New Knowledge discuss: honor chivalry, extend people's rights, establish societies, change institutions—even to abolishing kneeling and prostration, abolishing Manchu and Han scripts, leveling the honor between ruler and minister, and changing the separation of men and women inside and out."
translations.idiomatic: "As recent papers such as Current Affairs and New Knowledge discuss: honor chivalry, extend people's rights, establish societies, change institutions—even to abolishing kneeling and prostration, abolishing Manchu and Han scripts, leveling the honor between ruler and minister, and changing the separation of men and women inside and out."

sentences.zh: 直似只須中國一變而為外洋政教風俗，即可立致富強，而不知其勢小則群起鬥爭，立可召亂；

translations.literal: "It is as if China need only change at once into foreign government, teaching, and custom to become rich and strong at once, without knowing that on a small scale factions will rise and fight and disorder may be summoned at once;"
translations.idiomatic: "It is as if China need only change at once into foreign government, teaching, and custom to become rich and strong at once, without knowing that on a small scale factions will rise and fight and disorder may be summoned at once;"

sentences.zh: 大則各便私利，賣國何難？

translations.literal: "on a large scale each will seek private advantage—how hard to sell the state?"
translations.idiomatic: "on a large scale each will seek private advantage—how hard would it be to sell the state?"

sentences.zh: 曾以此言戒勸康有為，乃不思省改，且更私聚數百人，在輦轂之下，立為保國會，日執途人而號之曰：'中國必亡，必亡！

translations.literal: "I once admonished Kang Youwei with these words, yet he would not reflect and reform; instead he privately gathered several hundred men under the capital, established a Society to Protect the State, and daily seized passersby crying: 'China must perish, must perish!'"
translations.idiomatic: "I once admonished Kang Youwei with these words, yet he would not reflect and reform; instead he privately gathered several hundred men under the capital, established a Society to Protect the State, and daily seized passersby crying: 'China must perish, must perish!'"

sentences.zh: '以致士夫惶駭，庶眾搖惑。

translations.literal: "so that scholars were alarmed and the common people shaken."
translations.idiomatic: "So that scholars were alarmed and the common people shaken."

sentences.zh: 設使四民解體，大盜生心，藉此以集聚匪徒，招誘黨羽，因而犯上作亂，未知康有為又何以善其後？

translations.literal: "Suppose the four classes dissolve and great robbers take heart; using this to gather bandits and entice partisans, and thereby rebel against superiors—who knows how Kang Youwei would then set things right?"
translations.idiomatic: "Suppose the four classes dissolve and great robbers take heart; using this to gather bandits and entice partisans, and thereby rebel against superiors—who knows how Kang Youwei would then set things right?"

sentences.zh: 曾令其將忠君愛國合為一事，勿徒欲保中國而置我大清於度外，康有為亦似悔之。

translations.literal: "I once told him to join loyalty to the ruler and love of country in one matter and not merely wish to preserve China while setting our Great Qing outside consideration; Kang Youwei also seemed to repent."
translations.idiomatic: "I once told him to join loyalty to the ruler and love of country in one matter and not merely wish to preserve China while setting our Great Qing outside consideration; Kang Youwei also seemed to repent."

sentences.zh: 又曾手書御史名單一紙，欲臣倡首鼓動眾人伏闕痛哭，力請變法。

translations.literal: "He also once wrote out a list of censors by hand, wishing that I lead in stirring the multitude to kneel weeping at the palace gate and urgently plead for reform."
translations.idiomatic: "He also once wrote out a list of censors by hand, wishing that I lead in stirring the multitude to kneel weeping at the palace gate and urgently plead for reform."

sentences.zh: 當告以言官結黨為國朝大禁，此事萬不可為。

translations.literal: "I told him that censors forming factions is a great prohibition of our dynasty and this matter must on no account be done."
translations.idiomatic: "I told him that censors forming factions is a great prohibition of our dynasty and this matter must on no account be done."

sentences.zh: 以康有為一人在京城任意妄為，遍結言官，把持國事，已足駭人聽聞；

translations.literal: "That Kang Youwei alone in the capital acted wantonly, bound censors everywhere, and controlled state affairs is already enough to shock the ear;"
translations.idiomatic: "That Kang Youwei alone in the capital acted wantonly, bound censors everywhere, and controlled state affairs is already enough to shock the ear;"

sentences.zh: 而宋伯魯、楊深秀身為臺諫，公然聯名庇黨，誣參朝廷大臣，此風何可長也！

translations.literal: "and Song Bolu and Yang Shenxiu, themselves remonstrating officials, openly joined names to shield a faction and falsely impeached court ministers—how may this wind be allowed to grow!"
translations.idiomatic: "and Song Bolu and Yang Shenxiu, themselves remonstrating officials, openly joined names to shield a faction and falsely impeached court ministers—how may this wind be allowed to grow!"

sentences.zh: 伏思國家變法，原為整頓國事，非欲敗壞國事。

translations.literal: "I reflect that the state's reform was originally to put state affairs in order, not to ruin state affairs."
translations.idiomatic: "I reflect that the state's reform was originally to put state affairs in order, not to ruin state affairs."

sentences.zh: 譬如屋宇年久失修，自應招工依法改造，若任三五喜事之徒曳之傾倒，而曰非此不能從速，恐梁棟毀折，且將傷人。

translations.literal: "It is like a house long out of repair: one should hire workers to remodel it according to law; if one lets three or five men fond of novelty drag it down and say nothing else can be quick, I fear beams and rafters will break and people will be hurt."
translations.idiomatic: "It is like a house long out of repair: one should hire workers to remodel it according to law; if one lets three or five men fond of novelty drag it down and say nothing else can be quick, I fear beams and rafters will break and people will be hurt."

sentences.zh: 康有為之變法，何以異是？

translations.literal: "How is Kang Youwei's reform different from this?"
translations.idiomatic: "How is Kang Youwei's reform different from this?"

sentences.zh: 此所以不敢已於言也。

translations.literal: "This is why I dare not cease speaking."
translations.idiomatic: "This is why I dare not cease speaking."

sentences.zh: 」疏上，斥回原衙門行走。

translations.literal: "When the memorial was submitted, he was dismissed to serve in his original yamen."
translations.idiomatic: "When the memorial was submitted, he was dismissed to serve in his original yamen."

sentences.zh: 太后復訓政，賞文悌知府，旋授河南知府。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager resumed regency, Wen Ti was rewarded with the post of prefect and soon appointed prefect of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager resumed regency, Wen Ti was rewarded with the post of prefect and soon appointed prefect of Henan.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，兩宮西狩，文悌迎駕，擢貴西道。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, when the two palaces went west on campaign, Wen Ti welcomed the imperial progress and was promoted to Guixi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1900, when the two palaces fled west, Wen Ti welcomed the imperial progress and was promoted to Guixi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 乞病歸，卒。

translations.literal: He begged leave on illness and died.
translations.idiomatic: He begged leave on illness and died.

sentences.zh: 江春霖，字杏村，福建莆田人。

translations.literal: Jiang Chunlin, styled Xingcun, was a native of Putian in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Chunlin, styled Xingcun, was from Putian in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Guangxu he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In 1894 he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，轉御史，首論都御史陸寶忠幹煙禁，不宜為台長，劾親貴及樞臣疆臣，章凡數十上。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was made censor; he first argued that Censor-in-Chief Lu Baozhong, who handled the opium ban, was unfit to head the censorate, impeached imperial kin and grand councilors and frontier officials, and submitted several tens of memorials.
translations.idiomatic: In 1903 he was made censor; he first argued that Censor-in-Chief Lu Baozhong, who handled the opium ban, was unfit to head the censorate, impeached imperial kin and grand councilors and frontier officials, and submitted several tens of memorials.

sentences.zh: 德宗季葉，袁世凱出督畿輔，入贊樞廷，權勢傾一時。

translations.literal: In the late years of Dezong, Yuan Shikai went out to govern the capital region and entered the grand council; his power tilted the age.
translations.idiomatic: In the late years of Emperor Dezong, Yuan Shikai went out to govern the capital region and entered the grand council; his power tilted the age.

sentences.zh: 春霖獨論列十二事，謂：「洪範有言：'臣之有作威作福，其害於爾家，兇於爾國。

translations.literal: Chunlin alone set forth twelve matters, saying: "The Hongfan says: 'When ministers make might and blessings, it harms your house and is baleful to your state.'"
translations.idiomatic: Chunlin alone set forth twelve matters, saying: "The Hongfan says: 'When ministers make might and blessings, it harms your house and is baleful to your state.'"

sentences.zh: '左氏傳云：'受君之祿，是以聚黨，有黨而爭命，罪孰大焉？

translations.literal: "The Zuo Commentary says: 'Receiving the ruler's salary is thereby to gather a faction; having a faction and contending for command—what crime is greater?'"
translations.idiomatic: "The Zuo Commentary says: 'Receiving the ruler's salary is thereby to gather a faction; having a faction and contending for command—what crime is greater?'"

sentences.zh: '今世凱所為，其心即使無他，其跡要難共諒。

translations.literal: "What Shikai does today, even if his heart has no other intent, his tracks are hard to share in trust."
translations.idiomatic: "What Shikai does today, even if his heart has no other intent, his tracks are hard to share in trust."

sentences.zh: 歷考史冊所載權臣，大者貽憂君國，小者禍及身家。

translations.literal: "Examining the powerful ministers recorded in history, the great bring worry to ruler and state, the small bring disaster on themselves and their families."
translations.idiomatic: "Examining the powerful ministers recorded in history, the great bring worry to ruler and state, the small bring disaster on themselves and their families."

sentences.zh: 窺竊神器之徒，姑置勿論，即功在社稷，如霍光、李德裕、張居正，亦以權寵太盛，傾覆相尋。

translations.literal: "Those who stole the sacred vessel may be set aside; even those who served the altars of state, such as Huo Guang, Li Deyu, and Zhang Juzheng, because favor and power grew too great, downfall followed in turn."
translations.idiomatic: "Those who stole the sacred vessel may be set aside; even those who served the altars of state, such as Huo Guang, Li Deyu, and Zhang Juzheng, because favor and power grew too great, downfall followed in turn."

sentences.zh: 今不獨為國家計，宜加裁抑，即欲使世凱子孫長守富貴，亦不可無善處之法。

translations.literal: "Now, not only for the sake of the state should restraint be added; even if one wishes Shikai's descendants to long keep wealth and honor, there must be a good way to handle it."
translations.idiomatic: "Now, not only for the sake of the state should restraint be added; even if one wishes Shikai's descendants to long keep wealth and honor, there must be a good way to handle it."

sentences.zh: 」嗣是糾彈世凱及慶親王奕劻父子，連上八疏，皆不報，然朝貴頗嚴憚之。

translations.literal: "Thereafter he impeached Shikai and Prince Qing Yikuang father and son, submitting eight memorials in succession, all unanswered; yet the court nobles greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: "Thereafter he impeached Shikai and Prince Qing Yikuang father and son, submitting eight memorials in succession, all unanswered; yet the court nobles greatly feared him.

sentences.zh: 宣統改元，醇親王載灃既攝政，其弟載洵、載濤分長軍諮、海軍，頗用事。

translations.literal: When Xuantong began its reign, Prince Chun Zaifeng had become regent; his brothers Zaixun and Zaitao respectively headed the Army Advisory Council and the navy and wielded considerable power.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuantong began its reign, Prince Chun Zaifeng had become regent; his brothers Zaixun and Zaitao respectively headed the Army Advisory Council and the navy and wielded considerable power.

sentences.zh: 春霖謂：「古者鄭寵共叔，失教旋譏，漢驕厲王，不容終病，載在史冊，為萬世戒。

translations.literal: Chunlin said: "In antiquity, when Zheng favored Gongshu, loss of instruction brought swift reproach; when Han favored the arrogant Prince Li, he was not allowed to end his illness—these are recorded in the histories as warnings for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 論曰：有清列帝，家法最嚴，迨至季世，創制垂簾，於是閹寺漸肆，而親貴權要亦聲勢日著，雖有直言敢諫之士，無補危亡，亦盡其心焉而已。

translations.literal: The commentator says: The successive emperors of the Qing had the strictest house law; when the late age came and the institution of ruling from behind the curtain was created, eunuchs gradually grew wanton and imperial kin and powerful favorites also daily grew prominent in influence.
